steps.title: No hand-written boot script
steps.body: ST's default environment runs U-Boot's generic distro boot. The six steps on the left are what happens after U-Boot starts; the right side shows the one file it reads and what to check if it fails.

steps.title: 1. Where did we come from?
steps.body: U-Boot reads the ROM's boot context and sets `boot_device` (here `mmc`) and `boot_instance` (which SD/MMC controller), in `arch/arm/mach-stm32mp/stm32mp1/cpu.c`.

steps.title: 2. A one-second countdown
steps.body: After a one-second countdown (a keypress stops it and gives the `STM32MP> ` prompt), `bootcmd_stm32mp` prints `Boot over mmc0!`.

steps.title: 3. Only the device we booted from
steps.body: The script restricts the search to the card the firmware came from, then runs `distro_bootcmd`.

steps.title: 4. Which partition?
steps.body: U-Boot lists partitions with the GPT **bootable** flag (`part list mmc N -bootable`). With none it falls back to partition 1, which here is BL2, not a filesystem.

steps.title: 5. Which file?
steps.body: For each candidate it tries `<prefix>extlinux/extlinux.conf` with the prefixes `/` and `/boot/`. Finding one runs `sysboot`.

steps.title: 6. Load and start
steps.body: `sysboot` reads `extlinux.conf`, loads the `LINUX` file to `0xC2000000` and the `FDT` to `0xC4000000`, sets the command line from `APPEND` and `bootz` starts the kernel.

steps.anchor: If it does not boot, read the log
steps.title: If it does not boot
steps.body: The three lines to look for are `Scanning mmc 0:5...`, `Found /boot/extlinux/extlinux.conf` and `Retrieving file: /boot/zImage`. Stop autoboot to try the commands by hand.

steps.title: Why the bootable flag matters
steps.body: `image.sh` sets the GPT attribute bit 2 on the rootfs partition only. Without it U-Boot would scan partition 1, which holds BL2.
